title: Stamp gates: Proof strip
descriptionMd:
Inputs
`readings` is a list of integers (numbers with no decimal part). It may be empty, and numbers may repeat unless task 1 says otherwise.

Your tasks
1. Create a list `clamped`. Read `readings` from left to right. Change each number below 0 to 0. Keep every other number as it is. Put the numbers in `clamped` in the same order.
2. Complete `stampGatesProofStrip` so it returns `clamped`. Return it, do not print it.

Example
If `readings` is [8, 4, 6, -3, 6], then `clamped` is [8, 4, 6, 0, 6] and `stampGatesProofStrip` returns [8, 4, 6, 0, 6].

Rules
- If `clamped` is empty, return [].

Test data
TEST DATA 1: `readings` is [13, 0, -7, 4, 13].
TEST DATA 2: `readings` is [7, -6, 7, 7].
unitIntro: Read `readings` from left to right. Change each number below 0 to 0. Keep every other number as it is. Put the numbers in `clamped` in the same order. Each problem in this unit builds `clamped` first, then returns a different answer from it. Start with the first problem. The last problem also counts positions from 1.
constraints: Answers fit in a signed 32-bit integer: -2,147,483,648 through 2,147,483,647.
Input numbers have no decimal part. They range from -1,000,000 to 1,000,000. Follow any extra input rules in task 1.
Efficiency goal: time O(n); extra memory, including the helper list, O(n). n is the input length. These labels describe how work and memory grow with the input.
hints: Work through TEST DATA 1 by hand. Write down `clamped` before you look for the answer.
